summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with recurrent CNS lymphoma was admitted for his 19th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of reinduction therapy. He presented in stable condition with no acute symptoms and tolerated the infusion well. His hospital course was complicated by mild hyponatremia (sodium 127), managed with fluid restriction and temporary adjustment of desmopressin. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.08 by discharge. He remained neurologically stable, seizure-free, and hemodynamically normal. He was discharged home on his full regimen of home medications with follow-up scheduled in two weeks.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, lymph nodes of head, face, and neck
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
